newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese women turn to condoms as Valentine gift.
newsitem.headline: Japanese women turn to condoms as Valentine gift.

text.p: While chocolates remain the most popular Valentine"s Day gift in Japan, women are turning to a new way to express their love -- condoms.
"Condom sales around this time of the year are definitely increasing," said Koji Negishi, manager of Condomania, a condom speciality store in Tokyo.
Negishi said a gift set combining chocolate and condoms was selling particularly well among women in their twenties.
"It appears that girls are more frank than boys when giving the condoms as gifts," Negishi told Reuters.
"The men are often surprised but women see the condoms as something everybody uses," he said.
He said novelty items like fruit flavoured condoms and luminous models were the most popular.

"Valentine"s Day in Japan is usually marked by millions of women giving chocolates to the men in their lives, but this year a growing number of Japanese women have opted to give condoms as part of the ritual of affection," Kyodo News Service reported in its survey of what gifts people were giving.
In Japan, Valentine"s Day gifts are typically given by women. Men are expected to reciprocate a month later.
